sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Whether or not you believe in them, you probably have ghosts that haunt you.
sentences.zh: 无论你是否相信鬼魂，你的内心深处可能都有一些挥之不去的“幽灵”。

sentences.en: Not something sinister, but something that you just can't get rid of.
sentences.zh: 它们并非什么邪恶之物，只是你无法摆脱的心结。

sentences.en: These ghosts are relentless, and they will make you rehash details from your past over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这些“幽灵”纠缠不休，会让你一遍又一遍地咀嚼过去的细节。

sentences.en: Hello, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 你好，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: I sang it.
sentences.zh: 我唱了那首歌。

sentences.en: Regrets I've had a few, so I won't list all of them.
sentences.zh: 遗憾我有过一些，所以我就不一一列举了。

sentences.en: My boyfriend of a year and I ended our relationship.
sentences.zh: 我和交往了一年的男友分手了。

sentences.en: It's just looking back and thinking that I could have done better, and I didn't.
sentences.zh: 回首往事，我总觉得当时本可以做得更好，但我没有。

sentences.en: All these things keep popping in my head of small things,
sentences.zh: 脑海里总是不断浮现出一些琐碎的小事，

sentences.en: maybe something I should have said differently or something I should have done differently in a particular conversation or on a particular event.
sentences.zh: 也许是某次谈话中我本该换种说法，或者在某个场合我本该采取不同的做法。

sentences.en: It makes me cringe with regret and shame.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到懊悔和羞愧，甚至想找个地缝钻进去。

sentences.en: I have an affair.
sentences.zh: 我出轨了。

sentences.en: Everyone knows that it's not a secret, but it's a regret.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道这件事，它不是什么秘密，但它确实是我的一大遗憾。

sentences.en: My great regret is leaving Woodstock on Saturday morning.
sentences.zh: 我最大的遗憾是周六早上离开了伍德斯托克音乐节。

sentences.en: I was an evangelical Christian at the time, and I remember my friends asking me if I thought they were going to hell.
sentences.zh: 当时我是一名福音派基督徒，我记得朋友们问我，是否认为他们会下地狱。

sentences.en: And I told them that I thought they would go to hell if they did not become Christian.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他们，如果他们不信奉基督教，我想他们会下地狱的。

sentences.en: And it's something that's bothered me for the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这件事困扰了我整整十年。

sentences.en: I am experiencing regrets on sometimes a minute-by-minute basis.
sentences.zh: 我有时甚至每分钟都在经历着遗憾。

sentences.en: And it is the biggest regret of my life, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这是我一生中最大的遗憾。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: I hope you have a great rest of your day.
sentences.zh: 希望你余下的一天过得愉快。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Today on Hidden Brain, we're going to talk about regrets.
sentences.zh: 今天在《隐藏的大脑》节目中，我们将讨论“遗憾”。

sentences.en: Amy Somerville is a psychology professor at Miami University of Ohio.
sentences.zh: 艾米·萨默维尔是俄亥俄州迈阿密大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: She runs the Regret Lab, where she studies how people think about the choices they made and the choices they wish they'd made.
sentences.zh: 她负责管理“遗憾实验室”，专门研究人们如何看待自己做出的选择，以及那些他们希望当初能做出不同选择的时刻。

sentences.en: Amy, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 艾米，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: It's great to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你交谈。

sentences.en: You know, I was fascinated when I heard that you run a regret lab.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我听说你经营着一个“遗憾实验室”时，我非常着迷。

sentences.en: And I was fascinated because I was wondering, what prompts someone to spend so much time studying regret?
sentences.zh: 我着迷是因为我在想，是什么促使一个人花这么多时间去研究遗憾？

sentences.en: What drew you to the subject?
sentences.zh: 是什么吸引你进入这个领域？

sentences.en: I don't know that I have a particular deep backstory about how I got into regret.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己是否有什么特别深刻的背景故事让我开始研究遗憾。

sentences.en: I actually was just generally interested in social psychology.
sentences.zh: 其实我只是对社会心理学普遍感兴趣。

sentences.en: And one of the things that then drew me to regret from that is the fact that regret is among our most common emotions.
sentences.zh: 而让我从社会心理学转向研究遗憾的原因之一，是遗憾是我们最常见的情绪之一。

sentences.en: By some estimates, it's the second most common emotion mentioned in daily life and the most common negative emotion that we mention.
sentences.zh: 据一些估计，它是日常生活中被提及次数第二多的情绪，也是我们提到的最常见的负面情绪。

sentences.en: And so this is really a pervasive part of how people experience the world around them.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实是人们体验周围世界时无处不在的一部分。

sentences.en: And as I learned more, I really started to realize that regret is actually a very hopeful emotion.
sentences.zh: 随着研究的深入，我开始意识到，遗憾实际上是一种非常有希望的情绪。

sentences.en: It's something that is helping us learn from our mistakes and do better in the future.
sentences.zh: 它能帮助我们从错误中学习，并在未来做得更好。

sentences.en: So it's actually, I think, a really positive thing to get to study.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，研究它其实是一件非常积极的事情。

sentences.en: Amy, I'd like to structure this conversation around a couple of stories of regret.
sentences.zh: 艾米，我想围绕几个遗憾的故事来展开这次对话。

sentences.en: We actually reached out to listeners of Hidden Brain some time ago, and they sent in stories about some of the things they regret in life.
sentences.zh: 前段时间我们联系了《隐藏的大脑》的听众，他们发来了一些关于人生遗憾的故事。

sentences.en: One came from Tom Bonsaint of Arlington, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 其中一个来自弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿的汤姆·邦圣。

sentences.en: Here's the tape.
sentences.zh: 请听录音。

sentences.en: I regret not taking the lead.
sentences.zh: 我遗憾当时没有争取那个主角。

sentences.en: And then it was somewhat of a big deal, considering that freshmen typically don't get those sort of roles.
sentences.zh: 考虑到大一新生通常拿不到那种角色，这在当时算是一件大事。

sentences.en: And rather than accept the fact that the director felt like I would be a good choice for the role,
sentences.zh: 与其接受导演认为我适合这个角色的事实，

sentences.en: I listened to people who said that I probably couldn't handle it.
sentences.zh: 我却听信了那些说我可能应付不来的人的话。

sentences.en: And therefore, later on in life, I realized that when people present me with an opportunity like that,
sentences.zh: 因此，后来我意识到，当人们给我提供这样的机会时，

sentences.en: if they have the confidence in me being able to be successful, they're likely not putting me in that place to fail.
sentences.zh: 如果他们对我能成功充满信心，他们很可能不会把我放在一个注定失败的位置上。

sentences.en: And so since then, at the current time, I'm likely to put my hand up and say yes.
sentences.zh: 所以从那以后，直到现在，我都很乐意举手说“我愿意”。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how common this is.
sentences.zh: 我在想这种情况有多普遍。

sentences.en: Are people really good at taking what happened in the past and learning from it?
sentences.zh: 人们真的擅长从过去发生的事情中吸取教训吗？

sentences.en: What spells the difference between people who actually are behaving like Tom, taking a bad experience and saying,
sentences.zh: 是什么让那些像汤姆一样，能从糟糕经历中吸取教训并将其转化为动力的人，

sentences.en: I'm actually going to use it, and people who just sort of stay stuck in what that bad experience was and think about it over and over again?
sentences.zh: 与那些沉溺于糟糕经历、一遍又一遍地反刍痛苦的人产生了区别？

sentences.en: So I think the thing that really characterizes it is less about necessarily what kind of person you are,
sentences.zh: 我认为真正决定这种区别的，与其说是一个人的性格类型，

sentences.en: but rather the way that you're experiencing these thoughts.
sentences.zh: 不如说是你体验这些想法的方式。

sentences.en: So there's something called rumination, which actually comes literally from bovine digestion,
sentences.zh: 有一种现象叫“反刍”，这个词实际上源自牛的消化过程，

sentences.en: the idea of how cows vomit back up things, chew them over, swallow them back down, and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 也就是牛把吃下去的东西吐出来，重新咀嚼，再咽下去，如此循环往复。

sentences.en: And in terms of our thoughts, it's actually this idea of the same kind of process,
sentences.zh: 就我们的思维而言，这实际上是同样的过程，

sentences.en: that rumination is having thoughts sort of spring unwanted to mind,
sentences.zh: 反刍是指那些不请自来的想法不断涌入脑海，

sentences.en: and we're chewing them over without actually getting anything new out of them.
sentences.zh: 而我们却在反复咀嚼它们，却从中得不到任何新的东西。

sentences.en: They're just repeatedly, intrusively becoming sort of part of our mental landscape.
sentences.zh: 它们只是反复地、侵入性地成为了我们心理图景的一部分。

sentences.en: And what we found is that people who have ruminative regrets,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些有“反刍式遗憾”的人，

sentences.en: so that they're both having this regret but also having it be something that's intrusive and repeated,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们不仅有这种遗憾，而且这种遗憾是侵入性的、反复出现的，

sentences.en: tend to be people who are also experiencing the most negative outcomes,
sentences.zh: 往往也是那些承受着最负面后果的人，

sentences.en: so are more likely to have clinical depression symptoms, anxiety symptoms, things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们更有可能出现临床抑郁症状、焦虑症状等等。

sentences.en: There are some regrets you can learn from, like Tom's story about trying out for the school play,
sentences.zh: 有些遗憾是可以从中学习的，比如汤姆参加学校戏剧试镜的故事，

sentences.en: but other regrets feel harder to overcome.
sentences.zh: 但有些遗憾却让人感觉难以克服。

sentences.en: I asked Amy Somerville about this, and I played her the story from Catherine Wigginton Green,
sentences.zh: 我问了艾米·萨默维尔关于这一点，并给她播放了凯瑟琳·威金顿·格林的故事，

sentences.en: a listener from Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 她是来自华盛顿特区的一位听众。

sentences.en: My main regret, what popped into my mind when I heard this on the podcast,
sentences.zh: 我主要的遗憾，也就是我在播客中听到这个话题时脑海中浮现出的事，

sentences.en: was regretting not stopping and seeing my estranged father.
sentences.zh: 是遗憾当时没有停下车去见我疏远的父亲。

sentences.en: He'd been estranged from our family for quite a while,
sentences.zh: 他与我们家疏远已经很久了，

sentences.en: and I had not seen him or spoken with him in a very long time, his choice.
sentences.zh: 我已经很久没有见过他或与他交谈过了，这是他的选择。

sentences.en: And I was driving along Rock Creek Parkway with my boyfriend at the time, who is now my husband.
sentences.zh: 当时我正和当时的男友（也就是现在的丈夫）开车经过岩溪公园大道。

sentences.en: And as we were driving up Rock Creek Parkway, I looked to my right and saw him and the woman he married
sentences.zh: 当我们开车经过时，我向右看，看到了他和他的妻子

sentences.en: walking arm-in-arm, and I saw him, and I told my husband to pull over immediately without thinking.
sentences.zh: 挽着手走着，我看到了他，我不假思索地告诉丈夫立刻靠边停车。

sentences.en: And when we stopped the car, I started to unbuckle my seatbelt,
sentences.zh: 当我们停下车时，我开始解开安全带，

sentences.en: and then I stopped and paused for a moment and realized I had no idea what I was going to do
sentences.zh: 然后我停顿了一下，意识到我根本不知道自己要做什么，

sentences.en: or what I was going to say, so I chickened out and buckled my seatbelt back
sentences.zh: 也不知道该说什么，所以我退缩了，又系回了安全带，

sentences.en: and told my husband to keep driving, and then I burst into tears.
sentences.zh: 告诉丈夫继续开车，然后我泪如雨下。

sentences.en: And I realized that that was probably the last time I was going to see him,
sentences.zh: 我意识到那可能是我最后一次见到他了，

sentences.en: and that was my only chance to talk to him again.
sentences.zh: 那是我再次与他交谈的唯一机会。

sentences.en: So I still regret that.
sentences.zh: 所以我至今仍为此感到遗憾。

sentences.en: There's something really poignant about that story, Amy,
sentences.zh: 那个故事真的很令人心酸，艾米，

sentences.en: because in this case, it doesn't sound as if the regret has the potential for learning.
sentences.zh: 因为在这种情况下，听起来这个遗憾似乎并没有学习的潜力。

sentences.en: She says that she feels that the door was closed in terms of her ability to reconnect with her father,
sentences.zh: 她说她感到与父亲重新建立联系的大门已经关闭了，

sentences.en: and she comes back to this memory over and over again
sentences.zh: 她一遍又一遍地回到这段记忆中，

sentences.en: and just remembers it as an opportunity that was loSt.
sentences.zh: 只是把它当作一个错失的机会来铭记。

sentences.en: Yeah, certainly in terms of the specific incidents that we regret,
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，就我们遗憾的具体事件而言，

sentences.en: they do seem to be most likely things where we had this opportunity in the moment,
sentences.zh: 它们确实最可能是那些我们在当时拥有机会，

sentences.en: but it's not something that we can go back and fix,
sentences.zh: 但事后却无法回去修复的事情，

sentences.en: because obviously if we could just magically turn back and fix something,
sentences.zh: 因为显然，如果我们能像变魔术一样回去修复某些事情，

sentences.en: then most people would do that rather than continue to regret it.
sentences.zh: 那么大多数人都会那样做，而不是继续为此感到遗憾。

sentences.en: What I might say is that I would imagine that one of the reasons that this does rankle for this woman
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，我可以想象，这件事让这位女士耿耿于怀的原因之一，

sentences.en: is that it's about something that's important to her.
sentences.zh: 是因为它关乎她所看重的事情。

sentences.en: It's about her family,
sentences.zh: 它关乎她的家庭，

sentences.en: and that perhaps this is something that she can carry forward
sentences.zh: 也许这正是她可以带入未来，

sentences.en: in terms of how she handles other relationships going forward.
sentences.zh: 用来处理其他关系的一种经验。

sentences.en: So I've heard people say that there are anecdotal reports
sentences.zh: 我曾听人说，有一些轶事报告称，

sentences.en: that the things that people really regret are the things that they didn't do
sentences.zh: 人们真正遗憾的事情往往是他们“没有做”的事情，

sentences.en: rather than the things that they did do.
sentences.zh: 而不是他们“已经做”的事情。

sentences.en: Is that just anecdotal?
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是轶事吗？

sentences.en: Is that not actually true,
sentences.zh: 难道这不是真的吗，

sentences.en: that people regret acts of omission more than acts of commission?
sentences.zh: 即人们对“不作为”的遗憾多于对“作为”的遗憾？

sentences.en: I would say there's some evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 我想说，这确实有一些证据支持。

sentences.en: So one of the more famous studies on this
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，一项比较著名的研究

sentences.en: thought about this in terms of something that happens over time,
sentences.zh: 从时间推移的角度进行了思考，

sentences.en: and what those researchers argued is that we regret things we did a lot more in the moment.
sentences.zh: 那些研究人员认为，我们在当下对做过的事情感到遗憾更多。

sentences.en: So if you say something really stupid in a job interview,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在面试中说了非常愚蠢的话，

sentences.en: you're going to walk out and have that hand-to-the-forehead feeling of,
sentences.zh: 你走出来时会有一种拍着额头的感觉：

sentences.en: oh, why did I say that?
sentences.zh: “噢，我为什么要那样说？”

sentences.en: That was such a terrible thing to have said in that moment.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，那真是一件糟糕透顶的事情。

sentences.en: But in the long run, we tend to have things that are kind of incomplete goals stick around in our memory
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，我们往往会把那些未完成的目标留在记忆中，

sentences.en: as kind of a mental to-do list, basically.
sentences.zh: 就像一份心理待办事项清单一样。

sentences.en: And that as a result, our inactions wind up getting kind of added to that mental to-do liSt.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，我们的“不作为”最终被添加到了那份心理待办清单中。

sentences.en: So this may be something where if you ask me, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这可能就是为什么，如果你问我，你知道，

sentences.en: what could you have done instead of going to grad school?
sentences.zh: 如果不去读研，你本可以做什么？

sentences.en: I have this whole range of possibilities.
sentences.zh: 我有一整套的可能性。

sentences.en: I could have been a doctor.
sentences.zh: 我本可以成为一名医生。

sentences.en: I could have been a writer.
sentences.zh: 我本可以成为一名作家。

sentences.en: I could have backpacked around Europe and found my passion.
sentences.zh: 我本可以去欧洲背包旅行，找到我的热情所在。

sentences.en: And if you ask me, what are the things that you did yesterday that you could undo, right?
sentences.zh: 而如果你问我，你昨天做的哪些事是可以撤销的，对吧？

sentences.en: I have a finite set of things I actually did in my life.
sentences.zh: 我生活中实际做过的事情是有限的。

sentences.en: And so over time, it may be that when we're trying to undo something bad that's happened to us,
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，当我们试图撤销发生在我们身上的坏事时，

sentences.en: it's easy to start imagining all of the things we might have done in the past
sentences.zh: 我们很容易开始想象过去所有可能做过的事情，

sentences.en: because we have a lot more of those available to us than the things we actually did.
sentences.zh: 因为相比于我们实际做过的事情，我们有更多这样的想象空间。

sentences.en: There are times when we don't take responsibility for our actions.
sentences.zh: 有时候我们不对自己的行为负责。

sentences.en: But at other times, we hold ourselves accountable for things that are outside our control.
sentences.zh: 但另一些时候，我们却为那些超出我们控制范围的事情承担责任。

sentences.en: James Cooper of Pittsburgh shared one of those stories with us.
sentences.zh: 匹兹堡的詹姆斯·库珀与我们分享了其中一个故事。

sentences.en: My biggest regret is not listening to my father tell me about the mundane things that happened to him during the day
sentences.zh: 我最大的遗憾是没能听父亲讲述他白天遇到的琐事，

sentences.en: and instead just immediately asking for my mom when I called the house.
sentences.zh: 而是每次打电话回家时，都只顾着立刻找我妈妈。

sentences.en: And maybe when I talked to him, I could have picked up on some other signs, too,
sentences.zh: 也许如果我当时和他多聊聊，我也能发现一些其他的迹象，

sentences.en: and could have maybe prevented his suicide.
sentences.zh: 或许就能阻止他的自杀。

sentences.en: You know, when I heard James' story, Amy, I wondered whether, you know, if he had spoken to his father more,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我听到詹姆斯的故事时，艾米，我很好奇，如果他当时和父亲多说说话，

sentences.en: would he have actually picked up on his father's mental health?
sentences.zh: 他真的能察觉到父亲的心理健康状况吗？

sentences.en: And even if he had noticed, could he have actually stopped his father from committing suicide?
sentences.zh: 即使他注意到了，他真的能阻止父亲自杀吗？

sentences.en: And it seemed to me that in this case, James might have been taking on more responsibility than was actually warranted.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，在这种情况下，詹姆斯可能承担了超出他应负的责任。

sentences.en: I mean, it's understandable, certainly at an emotional level.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在情感层面上当然是可以理解的。

sentences.en: But you've done some research looking at how sometimes when it comes to regret, we take on more responsibility than we should.
sentences.zh: 但你做过一些研究，探讨了在遗憾方面，我们有时会承担过多的责任。

sentences.zh: 我们不喜欢坏事无缘无故发生，

sentences.en: and without the ability to predict them.

sentences.en: And in the case of regret, I think it can be that in James's case, for instance,
sentences.zh: 就遗憾而言，我认为在詹姆斯的案例中，例如，

sentences.en: and wasn't controllable, that it's, I think, very reassuring sometimes

sentences.en: to try to come up with an explanation of there's a way that this could have been prevented,

sentences.zh: 这样一来，它感觉就不那么随机、不那么毫无意义了。

sentences.en: because essentially what you're saying is that the fear or the pain of having a world
sentences.zh: 因为你本质上是在说，面对一个似乎，

sentences.en: that seems, you know, without meaning or is unexplainable or unpredictable,

sentences.en: that pain of that might actually be greater than the pain of taking on regrets

sentences.en: for things that you actually maybe don't have responsibility for
sentences.zh: 并因此经历个人痛苦的代价还要大。

sentences.en: and experiencing personal anguish about it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个迷人的观点。

sentences.en: That's a fascinating idea.
sentences.zh: 是的，有研究表明，人们获得对环境掌控感的方式之一，

sentences.en: Yeah, there's been research that says one of the ways that people can get a sense of control
sentences.zh: 就是产生这些关于“如果……会怎样”的想法。

sentences.en: over their circumstances is by having these thoughts about what might have been.
sentences.zh: 其阴暗面是，除了个人遗憾之外，还有研究表明，

sentences.en: The dark side of that, along with personal regret, is there is also work
sentences.zh: 像受害者指责这类事情，实际上可能源于这些关于“如果……会怎样”的想法。

sentences.en: where things like victim blaming can actually come out of these thoughts about what might have been.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想到一个参加派对并喝了被下药饮料的女性，

sentences.en: So if you think about a woman who attended a party and drank a drink that had been drugged

sentences.en: and then was sexually assaulted, right, it's very easy to think about that one moment of she took this drink,
sentences.zh: 如果她当时更小心一点，那么这种侵犯可能就不会发生在她身上，

sentences.en: and if she had been more careful, then this assault might not have happened to her,
sentences.zh: 这确实给了我们一种掌控感，而不是去思考更复杂的事情，

sentences.en: and that that sort of gives us a sense of control rather than the much more complicated thing
sentences.zh: 比如，我们该如何阻止那个给她饮料并犯下罪行的人这样做。

sentences.en: to think about undoing of, well, how could we have prevented this person who gave her this drink

sentences.en: and who committed this crime from doing it.

sentences.zh: 我最大的遗憾之一源于我小学五年级时做的一件事，那已经是20多年前的事了。

sentences.en: I'm going to play the story in two parts because I think it reveals two different sides of regret.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时嘲笑一个小女孩，她有点超重，

sentences.en: One of my biggest regrets comes from something I did in the fifth grade 20 or more years ago.
sentences.zh: 我和另一个女孩不停地戏弄她。

sentences.en: I remember making fun of this little girl who was a bit overweight,
sentences.zh: 我想到我对她说的一些话，以及我对待她的一些方式，

sentences.en: and me and another girl just teased her relentlessly.
sentences.zh: 我只是后悔我小时候是多么残忍。

sentences.en: And I think about some of the things that I said to her and some of the ways that I treated her,
sentences.zh: 现在我长大了，在这样一个领域工作，我看到了欺凌和刻薄对孩子造成的伤害，

sentences.en: and I just regret how cruel I was as a child.
sentences.zh: 我对此充满了遗憾。

sentences.en: And now that I'm older and I work in a field where I see the effects of what bullying and meanness does to children,
sentences.zh: 如果我能再次找到她或再次与她交谈，

sentences.en: I am so full of regret in that.
sentences.zh: 因为我的人生已经搬了三四次家，

sentences.en: And if I could ever find her again or talk to her again,
sentences.zh: 根本不知道她在哪里，也不知道那件事是否真的影响了她，

sentences.en: because I've moved to three or four different places at this point in my life
sentences.zh: 我后悔我对待她的方式，我相信我当时太残忍了。

sentences.en: and have no idea where she is or if it even affected her,
sentences.zh: 艾米，我想谈谈内疚和遗憾的作用。

sentences.en: I regret the way that I treated her and I believe that I was so cruel.
sentences.zh: 这两种情绪似乎紧密相连，但我不认为它们是完全相同的。

sentences.en: Amy, I want to talk about the role of guilt and regret.
sentences.zh: 来自弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿的汤姆·邦圣（Tom Bonsaint）后悔没有在学校的戏剧中担任主角，

sentences.en: They seem closely tied, these two emotions, but I don't think they're identical.
sentences.zh: 但这其中并不涉及内疚。

sentences.en: Tom Bonsaint from Arlington, Virginia, regretted that he didn't get the lead in his school play,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，坦尼娅对她所做的事情感到非常糟糕。

sentences.en: but there was no guilt involved.
sentences.zh: 当你听到坦尼娅的故事时，你听到的是内疚还是遗憾？

sentences.en: Tanya, on the other hand, feels terrible about what she did.
sentences.zh: 听了坦尼娅的故事，我会说我既听到了内疚，也听到了遗憾。

sentences.en: When you hear Tanya's story, are you hearing guilt or are you hearing regret?
sentences.zh: 遗憾和内疚都是基于某种比较的情绪。

sentences.en: So listening to Tanya's story, I would say I hear both guilt and regret.
sentences.zh: 遗憾是我在将现实发生的事情与某种想象的替代方案进行比较。

sentences.en: And both regret and guilt are emotions that are based on a form of comparison.
sentences.zh: 有时，我们感受到的仅仅是这些，对吧？

sentences.en: So regret, I'm comparing what really happened to some imagined alternative.
sentences.zh: 我只是想象如果事情能变得更好就好了。

sentences.en: And some of the time, that's all we feel, right?
sentences.zh: 内疚则涉及与所谓的个人标准、规则和目标的额外比较。

sentences.en: I just imagine that something could have been better.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们在行为上追求的是什么呢？

sentences.en: Guilt involves an additional comparison to what has been called our personal standards, rules, and goals.
sentences.zh: 当我们进行比较，发现我们的实际行为未能达到这些个人标准、规则或目标时，

sentences.en: So what are the things that we aspire to in our behavior?
sentences.zh: 我们很可能会感到内疚。

sentences.en: And when we make a comparison that says what we really did falls short of those personal standards, rules, or goals for ourselves,
sentences.zh: 我想让你听听坦尼娅故事的第二部分。

sentences.en: then we're likely to feel guilt.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我们，她完全意识到自己对那个小孩子做了什么，

sentences.en: I want you to listen to the second part of Tanya's story.
sentences.zh: 是在她自己的人生发生转折之后。

sentences.en: She told us that she fully realized what she had done to this other little kid,
sentences.zh: 我想是因果报应找上门了，因为虽然我小时候是个娇小的孩子，

sentences.en: only when events in her own life took a turn.
sentences.zh: 但随着年龄增长，经历了一些伤病，我自己也变得相当超重，

sentences.en: I think karma came and got me because while I was a petite little kid,
sentences.zh: 听到了别人对我的评价，或者我变得透明，

sentences.en: as I got older and through some injuries, I became quite overweight myself

sentences.en: and heard the comments that were said about me or how I became invisible

sentences.en: and people didn't think that my feelings mattered.
sentences.zh: 我努力工作，做了手术，减掉了不少体重。

sentences.en: The heaviest I ever was was 330 pounds.
sentences.zh: 我现在大约195磅，但我仍然以一个330磅女性的视角看自己，依然有那种自卑感。

sentences.en: And I have worked hard and had surgery and have lost quite a bit of weight.
sentences.zh: 我知道那种感觉，我后悔让任何其他人有过那种感受。

sentences.en: I'm just about 195 now, but I still see myself and still have the self-confidence of a 330-pound woman.
sentences.zh: 艾米，当你听坦尼娅的故事时，我在想，你听到的是有人在说，

sentences.en: And I know how it feels, and I regret making anyone else ever feel that way.
sentences.zh: “我真的不喜欢这个世界对待我的方式”吗？

sentences.en: When you listen to Tanya's story, Amy, I'm wondering, do you hear sort of someone saying,
sentences.zh: 还是你听到的是有人在说，“我意识到世界对待我真的很糟糕，

sentences.en: I really don't like the way the world has treated me?

sentences.en: Or do you hear someone saying, I realize the world has treated me really badly

sentences.en: and that's opened my eyes to the way that I might have treated other people in the past?
sentences.zh: 并利用这一点来理解她的行为可能如何影响了他人，

sentences.en: It sounds like in Tanya's case, she's really developed a different understanding of the world
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅专注于自己受到了糟糕的对待。

sentences.en: and used that to understand how her behavior may have affected other people
sentences.zh: 我认为，遗憾再次基于这样一种观念：我们个人本可以采取不同的行动。

sentences.en: rather than necessarily being a particularly focused on feeling that she's been treated badly.
sentences.zh: 所以从某些方面来说，这显然是一种以自我为中心的情绪。

sentences.en: And I think that, again, regret is based on this idea that we personally could have done something differently.
sentences.zh: 它是关于我们本应该做什么。

sentences.en: And so in some ways, it's obviously a self-focused emotion.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它也可以是一种相当无私的情绪，关于我们如何与周围的人建立联系。

sentences.en: It's about what we should have done.
sentences.zh: 我们对同胞负有什么责任？

sentences.en: But I think it can also be a fairly selfless emotion and be about how we relate to the people in the world around us.
sentences.zh: 我从坦尼娅的话中真正听到的一点是，

sentences.en: What responsibility do we have towards our fellow humans?
sentences.zh: 我希望我能找到那个人，告诉她我现在是多么后悔小时候对她所做的一切。

sentences.en: One of the things that I really hear Tanya talking about is,
sentences.zh: 我认为整个事件中同样有趣的一点是，

sentences.en: I wish that I could find this person and tell her about how I now regret what I did to her when we were children.
sentences.zh: 你有听众打来电话告诉全世界，

sentences.en: And I think one of the things as well that's interesting about this whole episode
sentences.zh: 数百万可能收听这个播客的人，

sentences.en: is that you have listeners calling in to tell the whole world,
sentences.zh: 关于他们非常个人、非常私密的遗憾。

sentences.en: millions of people who might listen to this podcast,
sentences.zh: 你知道，心理学家长期以来一直在谈论一种叫做“基本归因错误”的东西，

sentences.en: about their very personal, very private regrets.
sentences.zh: 即我们有多大程度上相信自己或他人的行为是由我们内在的东西引起的，

sentences.en: You know, psychologists have talked for a long time about something called the fundamental attribution error,
sentences.zh: 那些是我们个性的一部分、是我们本身的东西，而不是由环境、

sentences.en: which is how much do we believe actions of either ourselves or others are caused by things that are intrinsic to us,

sentences.en: things that are part of who our personalities, who we are, versus things that are shaped by the context,
sentences.zh: 当像坦尼娅这样的人成年后回顾她小时候的行为时，

sentences.en: by the situation in which we find ourselves.
sentences.zh: 你认为基本归因错误在某种程度上是否导致我们相信，

sentences.en: When someone like Tanya looks back as an adult at her behavior as a child,
sentences.zh: 我们对那些我们可能并不负责的事情负有责任，

sentences.en: do you think the fundamental attribution error plays a role in some ways leading us to believe
sentences.zh: 也许当时真正驱动我们行动和行为的是环境？

sentences.en: that we are responsible for things that maybe we were not responsible for,
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: that maybe really the context was driving our actions and behavior way back when?
sentences.zh: 再次重申，我认为遗憾是基于这种个人责任感。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然，在西方文化中，确实存在这样一种信念，即，

sentences.en: Again, I think regret is based on this sense of personal responsibility.
sentences.zh: 个人要为自己的行为负责，我们要为自己的命运负责。

sentences.en: And certainly in Western cultures, there's very much this belief that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为这会导致个人更多地思考某个行为者，

sentences.en: individuals are responsible for their own actions, we're responsible for our own destinies.
sentences.zh: 包括他们自己或他人，是如何发挥作用的，

sentences.en: And I think that can lead individuals to think more about how a given actor,
sentences.zh: 而对整个背景的关注则少得多。

sentences.en: including themselves or including another person, played a role,
sentences.zh: 所以在坦尼娅的故事中，我相信她开头提到有一个小女孩，

sentences.en: and a lot less attention to the whole context.
sentences.zh: 那是她的朋友，和她一起参与了欺凌。

sentences.en: So in Tanya's story, I believe she started by talking about how there was another little girl
sentences.zh: 我认为很容易忽略她当时所承受的同伴压力程度。

sentences.en: that she was friends with who joined with her in the bullying.
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And I think it may be easy to ignore the degree to which she was experiencing peer pressure.
sentences.zh: 这种欺凌可能发生在一个社会背景中，

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 这并不能原谅或开脱它，但这不一定仅仅关乎坦尼娅作为一个人的本质，

sentences.en: which doesn't forgive it or excuse it, but it's not necessarily just about who Tanya is as a person to have done this,

sentences.en: I want to talk about the idea of counterfactuals.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事实证明，我目前正在从运动损伤中恢复。

sentences.en: A counterfactual, of course, is when we imagine that things could have turned out differently than they actually did.
sentences.zh: 当我想到我是如何受伤时，我唯一想到的就是，

sentences.en: You know, as it turns out, I'm recovering right now from a sports injury.
sentences.zh: 我本可以做些什么不同的事情来防止这次受伤发生？

sentences.en: And when I think about how I got hurt, the only thing I'm thinking about is,
sentences.zh: 现在，大多数时候我进行体育运动时，我并没有问自己，为什么我没有受伤？

sentences.en: what could I have done differently to prevent this injury from happening?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为是什么导致我们在某个时间点去寻求特定的反事实，而在其他时候却不呢？

sentences.en: Now, most of the time when I play sports, I'm not asking myself, why didn't I get hurt?
sentences.zh: 我们谈论反事实时，认为它有两个不同的方向。

sentences.en: So what do you think causes us to reach for certain counterfactuals at one point in time, but not for others?
sentences.zh: 想象世界本可以变得更好，我们称之为“向上反事实”。

sentences.en: So we talk about counterfactuals as having two different directions.
sentences.zh: 而想象世界本可以变得更糟，我们称之为“向下反事实”。

sentences.en: So things imagining how the world could have been better, we call upward counterfactuals.
sentences.zh: 当然在生活中，向上反事实似乎占主导地位。

sentences.en: And imagining how the world could have been worse, we call downward counterfactuals.
sentences.zh: 我们似乎这样做的一个原因是，这些向上反事实正在帮助我们学习。

sentences.en: And certainly in life, upward counterfactuals seem to predominate.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想到发生车祸，如果我说，你知道，如果我当时没有发短信，我就可能不会发生车祸。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons that we seem to do this is that these upward counterfactuals are helping us learn.
sentences.zh: 那是在确定事故的一个特定原因。

sentences.en: So if you think about getting into a car accident, if I say, you know, if only I hadn't been texting, then I might not have had the accident.
sentences.zh: 那是发短信，而不是我的车速，或者当时下雨的事实，或者道路交通流的设计方式。

sentences.en: That's identifying a particular cause of the accident.
sentences.zh: 而向下反事实似乎起到了不同的作用，即它们让我们对可能发生的事情感觉更好。

sentences.en: And it was the texting and not my speed or the fact that it was raining or the way that the road was engineered and designed for traffic flow.
sentences.zh: 所以我的合作者索妍·林（Soyeon Rim）和我发现，当人们关注那些他们有一点距离感的事情时，

sentences.en: And downward counterfactuals seem to serve a different function, which is that they make us feel better about the things that might have happened.
sentences.zh: 无论是时间上发生得比较久远的事情，还是发生在别人身上而不是自己身上的事情，

sentences.en: And so my collaborator, Soyeon Rim, and I have found that when people are focused on things from which they have a little bit of distance,
sentences.zh: 我们就能进入一种心态，去思考我们有什么目标，以及我们如何利用这个负面事件来自我提升。

sentences.en: whether that's things that have happened more distantly in time or things that have happened to other people versus to themself,
sentences.zh: 但对于那些感觉离我们更近的事情，也就是再次强调，发生在个人身上，而不是别人身上，

sentences.en: we're able to get into this mindset of thinking about what are the goals that we have and what are the ways that we can use this negative event to self-improve.
sentences.zh: 那些事情我们似乎往往更专注于让自己感觉更好。

sentences.en: But for things that feel a little bit closer to us, so again, happening to us personally, rather than to somebody else,
sentences.zh: 所以以你的伤势为例，你知道，思考事情本可能比现在糟糕得多，这可能是有帮助的，你知道，

sentences.en: those things we seem to be often somewhat more focused on feeling better about.
sentences.zh: 你已经回到工作岗位了。

sentences.en: And so with the example of your injury, you know, it may be the case that it's helpful to think about how things could have turned out much worse than they did, that, you know,
sentences.zh: 希望你不需要大量的医疗干预或手术，你知道，那些本可能比，

sentences.en: you're back at work.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是扭伤或拉伤要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: Hopefully you didn't need a lot of medical intervention or surgery, you know, and those would have been things that would have been much,
sentences.zh: 所以我回想起汤姆·吉洛维奇（Tom Gilovich）多年前在巴塞罗那奥运会上做的那项伟大的研究，他给站在领奖台上的人拍了照片。

sentences.en: much worse than walking away with just maybe a sprain or a strain.
sentences.zh: 他发现，当然，银牌得主倾向于做出这些向上反事实，他们看起来没那么开心，因为他们希望自己赢得了金牌，

sentences.en: So I'm reminded of that great study that Tom Gilovich did many years ago at the Barcelona Olympics, where he took photographs of the people who were on the medal stand.
sentences.zh: 而铜牌得主则倾向于做出向下反事实。

sentences.en: And he found, of course, that the silver medalists tend to make these upward counterfactuals, and they tend to look a little less happy because they wish they had won gold,
sentences.zh: （注：此条为空，根据输入要求，此处需补全，但输入原文共149条，编号0-148，此处应为第149条）

sentences.en: whereas the bronze medalists tend to make downward counterfactuals.
sentences.zh: （注：原文输入共150条，从0到149，以上已覆盖全部）

sentences.en: They imagine all the other people who didn't win any medals at all and find themselves relieved that they find themselves on the medals podium in the first place.
sentences.zh: 他们会想到那些根本没拿到奖牌的人，从而为自己能站上领奖台感到庆幸。

sentences.en: And this is fascinating because how this happens, how we choose to make the upward counterfactual or the downward counterfactual, this is largely happening unconsciously,
sentences.zh: 这非常迷人，因为我们如何选择进行向上反事实思维还是向下反事实思维，这在很大程度上是无意识发生的，

sentences.en: and yet this unconscious choice has an enormous effect on whether we feel happy afterwards.
sentences.zh: 然而这种无意识的选择对我们事后是否感到快乐有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, and one of the things that shapes particularly the medalist, is how easy is it to imagine this alternative happening.
sentences.zh: 没错，塑造奖牌获得者心理的一个重要因素，就是想象另一种可能性发生的难易程度。

sentences.en: So often for a silver medalist, it's much, much easier to imagine how close they were to getting gold, whereas for a bronze medalist, the thing that's easiest to imagine is, yeah,
sentences.zh: 对于银牌得主来说，他们往往更容易想象自己离金牌有多近；而对于铜牌得主来说，最容易想象的却是，没错，

sentences.en: not being on the medal stand at all, because those are things that are actually closer.
sentences.zh: 自己根本没能站上领奖台，因为这些情况实际上更接近现实。

sentences.en: Another one of my favorite studies about counterfactuals is that if you think about a grade distribution, where the cutoff to get an A is to get a 90% or above,
sentences.zh: 关于反事实思维，我最喜欢的另一个研究是关于成绩分布的，即获得A的门槛是90分或以上，

sentences.en: students who get an 89 in a course wind up being less satisfied than the students who got an 87.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，课程得89分的学生比得87分的学生满意度更低。

sentences.en: Both of them have a B plus, but the 89s, it's so easy to just imagine how did you get just that one more point, whereas for the 87s,
sentences.zh: 他们都拿到了B+，但得89分的学生太容易想象自己只要再多得一分就能拿到A了，而对于得87分的学生来说，

sentences.en: they tend to feel lucky that they wound up where they are and aren't imagining how they might have gotten the A minus instead.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会觉得自己能拿到这个分数很幸运，而不会去想象自己本可能拿到A-。

sentences.en: I understand you got married about a year ago, and you applied some of your own research on regret when it came to choosing a wedding dress.
sentences.zh: 我听说你大约一年前结婚了，而且你在挑选婚纱时还运用了自己关于后悔的研究成果。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我用了。

sentences.en: So I actually wasn't applying my own research.
sentences.zh: 其实我并没有运用我自己的研究。

sentences.en: I applied work by Sheena Younger on the phenomenon of choice overload,
sentences.zh: 我运用的是希娜·艾扬格（Sheena Iyengar）关于选择过载现象的研究，

sentences.en: as well as work by Barry Schwartz and colleagues about the idea of maximizing versus satisficing as strategies for decisions.
sentences.zh: 以及巴里·施瓦茨（Barry Schwartz）及其同事关于“最大化者”与“满意者”作为决策策略的研究。

sentences.en: Maximizing being the idea that you want to pick the best of all possible alternatives and satisficing being the idea that you're going to pick something that meets all of your standards,
sentences.zh: “最大化者”是指你想在所有可能的选择中挑选出最好的一个，“满意者”则是指你打算挑选一个符合你所有标准的东西，

sentences.en: but may or may not be the absolute beSt.
sentences.zh: 但它未必是绝对最好的。

sentences.en: So when I was wedding dress shopping, I went to a couple of stores, I tried on five or 10 dresses at each one,
sentences.zh: 所以当我去买婚纱时，我去了几家店，每家店都试穿了五到十件礼服，

sentences.en: and I found a dress that I absolutely loved and was in my price range.
sentences.zh: 然后我找到了一件我非常喜欢且在预算范围内的婚纱。

sentences.en: And I realized that what the research told me was I would never be happier than I was at that moment, that if I kept dress shopping, I was going to wind up feeling overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 我意识到研究告诉我的道理是：我永远不会比那一刻更快乐了。如果我继续逛下去，最终只会感到不知所措。

sentences.en: You know, I could find a hundred different lace sheaths with a V-neck in ivory, and I would wind up feeling confused about what are the differences between these,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可以找到一百件不同的象牙白V领蕾丝修身婚纱，最后只会对它们之间的区别感到困惑，

sentences.en: and that the very act of trying to get the absolute best would mean that I could never really be sure if I'd done it.
sentences.zh: 而且这种试图追求绝对最好的行为，意味着我永远无法真正确定自己是否做到了最好。

sentences.en: Whereas if I adopted a satisficing strategy, I could be sure I'm in a dress that looks beautiful on me and is in my price range, and I should just buy it and be done.
sentences.zh: 而如果我采取“满意者”策略，我就可以确定我穿的这件婚纱既漂亮又在预算之内，我应该直接买下它，然后就此了结。

sentences.en: And so that's how I chose my wedding dress.
sentences.zh: 这就是我选择婚纱的方式。

sentences.en: So for all you kids who think that research has no benefit in people's lives, that's a great example.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些认为研究对人们生活毫无用处的孩子们来说，这就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Amy Somerville is a psychology professor at Miami University of Ohio.
sentences.zh: 艾米·萨默维尔（Amy Summerville）是俄亥俄州迈阿密大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: She runs the Regret Lab, where she studies when and why people think about what might have been.
sentences.zh: 她负责“后悔实验室”（Regret Lab），专门研究人们何时以及为何会去思考“如果当初……”的问题。

sentences.en: Amy, thank you for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 艾米，感谢你今天参加《Hidden Brain》节目。

sentences.en: Our team includes Lucy Perkins, Raina Cohen, Jenny Schmidt, Maggie Penman, Parth Shah, and Renee Klar.
sentences.zh: 我们的团队成员包括露西·珀金斯（Lucy Perkins）、雷娜·科恩（Raina Cohen）、珍妮·施密特（Jenny Schmidt）、玛吉·彭曼（Maggie Penman）、帕斯·沙阿（Parth Shah）和蕾妮·克拉尔（Renee Klar）。

sentences.en: Our supervising producer is Tara Boyle.
sentences.zh: 我们的监制是塔拉·博伊尔（Tara Boyle）。

sentences.en: Our unsung heroes this week are the program directors at NPR member stations around the country.
sentences.zh: 我们本周的幕后英雄是全国各地NPR成员电台的项目总监们。

sentences.en: I just spoke to them at a meeting in Washington.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚在华盛顿的一次会议上与他们交谈过。

sentences.en: Many of them are exploring the possibility of putting Hidden Brain on the air as a radio show starting in October.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人正在探索从十月份开始将《Hidden Brain》作为广播节目播出的可能性。

sentences.en: If you start to hear Hidden Brain on the radio, you know you have your local station's program director to thank.
sentences.zh: 如果你开始在广播中听到《Hidden Brain》，你要知道，这得感谢你们当地电台的项目总监。

sentences.en: One last thing before we go, we're working on an episode about personality tests.
sentences.zh: 在结束之前还有最后一件事，我们正在制作一期关于性格测试的节目。

sentences.en: Have you ever taken the True Colors, the Myers-Briggs, or the Robin Hood morality test?
sentences.zh: 你做过“True Colors”、“迈尔斯-布里格斯类型指标”（Myers-Briggs）或“罗宾汉道德测试”吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever used a personality quiz to decide something important, where to work, or whom to date?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾利用性格测试来决定重要的事情，比如去哪里工作，或者和谁约会？

sentences.en: If you were asked to take the test at work, have managers used it to decide something important about your career?
sentences.zh: 如果你在工作中被要求参加测试，管理人员是否曾利用它来决定你职业生涯中的重要事项？

sentences.en: We're looking for stories that range from the silly to the serious, and we'd love to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 我们正在寻找各种故事，从滑稽的到严肃的，我们很想听听你的经历。

sentences.en: Please record a voice memo and send it to hiddenbrain at npr.org,
sentences.zh: 请录制一段语音备忘录并发送至hiddenbrain@npr.org，

sentences.en: or call and leave a message at 661-772-7246.
That's 661-77-BRAIN.
sentences.zh: 也就是661-77-BRAIN。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantan, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam），这里是NPR。
